verdicts.evidence: Re-measured 2026-09-29 and re-filed from `hole` (COULD NOT CLEAR) to `equivalent`. `j?.loop_count` -> `j.loop_count` differs only when JSON.parse returns null, and then the mutated read throws a TypeError INSIDE the surrounding try, whose catch returns `{ alreadyBlocked: false, loopCount: null }`, exactly what the optional chain produces for null (undefined is not a number, and `undefined === true` is false). Every other parse result (a number, a string, true, an array, an object) is property-readable, so both builds read the same value. Measured: parseHookPayload on 17 payloads (empty, null, true, 0, 1, a string, [], {}, the two guards with right and wrong types, loop_count null, garbage, a __proto__ key) returns byte-identical results on both builds, and the command-level probe of 2026-09-28 (gate-hook for three harnesses on eleven missions, stdin `{}`) is byte-identical. Survived the CI unit pass on this branch and the whole-net pass of 2026-09-29.
